connections.why: Observational records become the raw material for developing ideas
Ideas are realised by choosing appropriate techniques and media
Mastering techniques deepens proficiency in handling materials
Skilled handling of materials strengthens a piece's visual impact
Evaluating work tells the artist how to refine it for greater impact
Critical reflection feeds back into developing new ideas
Studying others' work builds the critical vocabulary used to evaluate one's own
Knowing art history situates individual artists within movements and periods
Knowledge of styles and movements inspires and informs pupils' own ideas
Studying practitioners reveals the techniques and media they pioneered
Observational drawing develops the mark-making techniques used throughout
Refining outcomes prompts new directions for further creative work
